title: ASP.NET Core Complete Cheat Sheet
description: Comprehensive reference for ASP.NET Core MVC and Web API: project structure, controllers, routing, model binding, validation, Razor views, tag helpers, middleware, DI, configuration, EF Core, filters, auth, CORS, responses, areas, session, caching, error handling, logging, file uploads, content negotiation, API versioning, rate limiting, health checks, SignalR, background services, and more.

data.text: Project Structure and Program.cs

ASP.NET Core 7+ uses the minimal hosting model. `Program.cs` registers services via `builder.Services`, builds the middleware pipeline, and calls `app.Run()`. Environment-specific setup is handled via `IHostEnvironment` or `IWebHostEnvironment`.

data.title: Program.cs with Environment-Aware Setup
Top-Level Statements and Builder Pattern

data.text: MVC Controllers

Inherit from `Controller` when rendering views. It provides view-related features like `View()`, `ViewData`, `ViewBag`, and `TempData`. Use `ControllerBase` for APIs or when you do not need view support.

data.title: MVC Controller with View Results
ControllerBase for Web API

data.text: Web API Controllers
The `[ApiController]` attribute enables automatic 400 responses for invalid models, binding-source inference, and Swagger metadata. Use DTOs instead of exposing domain entities directly.

data.title: ApiController Attribute and DTOs

data.text: Routing
Conventional routing maps URL patterns in `Program.cs`. Attribute routing places route templates directly on controllers and actions. Combine both for flexible URL structures.

data.title: Conventional and Attribute Routing
Route Tokens, Constraints, and URL Generation

data.text: Model Binding

Model binding maps incoming request data to action parameters. Binding-source attributes like `[FromBody]`, `[FromQuery]`, `[FromRoute]`, `[FromForm]`, and `[FromHeader]` control where data is read from.

data.title: Binding Sources and Complex Types
Custom Model Binder Example

data.text: Validation

Data annotations provide declarative validation. `[ApiController]` automatically returns 400 with validation details. For complex rules, implement `IValidatableObject` or create custom `ValidationAttribute` classes.

data.title: Data Annotations and IValidatableObject

data.text: Razor Views Basics
Razor views use `.cshtml` files with C# code embedded in HTML. The `@model` directive declares the strongly-typed model. Use `@{}` for code blocks and `@Html` helpers for form generation.

data.title: Strongly Typed Razor View
ViewData, ViewBag, and TempData

data.text: Tag Helpers
Tag Helpers enhance HTML elements with server-side behavior. Built-in helpers cover forms, inputs, links, and validation. Create custom tag helpers for reusable components.

data.title: Built-in Tag Helpers
data.code:
@model Product
Cancel
@await Component.InvokeAsync("ProductSummary", new { id = 5 })

data.title: Custom Tag Helper

data.text: Middleware Pipeline

Middleware processes each request and response. Order matters: authentication must come before authorization. Use `Use` for next-middleware chains, `Run` for terminal middleware, and `Map` for branching pipelines.

data.title: Middleware Ordering and Custom Middleware

data.text: Dependency Injection
ASP.NET Core DI supports `Transient`, `Scoped`, and `Singleton` lifetimes. Constructor injection is preferred. Use factories for dynamic resolution and `IServiceProvider` for late-bound services.

data.title: Service Lifetimes and Constructor Injection

data.text: Configuration and Options

ASP.NET Core reads configuration from `appsettings.json`, `appsettings.{Environment}.json`, environment variables, user secrets, and command-line args. The options pattern binds configuration sections to strongly typed classes.

data.title: appsettings.json and Options Pattern

data.text: Entity Framework Core Basics
EF Core is the standard ORM. Define `DbSet<T>` properties in `DbContext`, configure with Fluent API or data annotations, and use LINQ for queries. Eager loading uses `Include`.

data.title: DbContext, DbSet, and CRUD with LINQ

data.text: Filters

Filters run code before or after pipeline stages: authorization, resources, action execution, results, and exceptions. Register globally, per-controller, or per-action using `ServiceFilter` or `TypeFilter`.

data.title: Action, Exception, and Resource Filters

data.text: Authentication and Authorization

Use `[Authorize]` to protect endpoints. Configure authentication schemes (JWT, cookies) in `Program.cs`. Policies, roles, and claims provide fine-grained access control. ASP.NET Core Identity is the full membership system.

data.title: JWT Bearer Authentication and Policies
Cookie Authentication and Identity Overview

data.text: CORS
Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) controls which origins can call your API. Define named policies with specific origins, methods, and headers. Place `UseCors` in the correct pipeline order.

data.title: CORS Policies and Placement

data.text: Response Types and Status Codes
Return proper HTTP status codes using `IActionResult` helpers. `ActionResult<T>` combines typed responses with status codes. `ProblemDetails` is the standard RFC 7807 error format.

data.title: Standard Status Code Responses

data.text: Areas
Areas partition large MVC apps into feature groups with their own controllers, views, and routes. Enable area routing with `{area:exists}` in conventional route patterns.

data.title: Area Setup and Route Pattern

data.text: Session and Cache

Use `ISession` for per-user session state. Use `IMemoryCache` for in-process caching. Add distributed cache for multi-server deployments. Response caching reduces server load for static-ish responses.

data.title: Session, Memory Cache, and Response Caching

data.text: Error Handling

Use `UseExceptionHandler` for production error handling. Developer Exception Page is for development only. `StatusCodePages` handles non-success HTTP responses. ProblemDetailsFactory creates RFC 7807 error bodies.

data.title: Exception Handling and ProblemDetails

data.text: Logging
ASP.NET Core includes a built-in logging abstraction. Use `ILogger<T>` for structured logging. Configure providers and log levels in `appsettings.json`.

data.title: ILogger and Structured Logging

data.text: File Upload
Accept uploaded files via `IFormFile` for small files or stream them directly for large uploads. Always validate file type and size. Configure `RequestSizeLimit` for larger payloads.

data.title: IFormFile and Streaming Upload

data.text: Content Negotiation
Content negotiation selects the response format based on the `Accept` header. ASP.NET Core includes JSON and XML formatters. Configure JSON options or add custom formatters for other media types.

data.title: JSON Options and Produces Attribute

data.text: API Versioning
API versioning lets you evolve APIs without breaking existing clients. Use URL path, query string, header, or media type versioning. Mark old versions as deprecated.

data.title: URL Path and Query String Versioning

data.text: Rate Limiting
ASP.NET Core 7+ includes built-in rate limiting. Use fixed window, sliding window, or concurrency limits. Define policies in `Program.cs` and attach them with `[EnableRateLimiting]`.

data.title: Rate Limiting Policies

data.text: Health Checks

Health checks report the health of app dependencies. Use built-in checks for databases, add custom checks, and optionally expose a UI. Health checks are commonly used by load balancers and orchestrators.

data.title: Health Checks Configuration

data.text: SignalR Basics

SignalR enables real-time server-to-client communication. Define a Hub class, call `SendAsync` on clients, and handle connection lifecycle events. The JavaScript client connects and invokes server methods.

data.title: SignalR Hub and JavaScript Client

data.text: Background Services
Run background tasks using `IHostedService` or inherit from `BackgroundService`. Use `BackgroundService` for long-running loops. Queue work items from requests for reliable processing.

data.title: BackgroundService and Queued Hosted Service

data.text: Partial Views and View Components
Partial views render reusable view fragments. View Components are like mini-controllers with logic and views, ideal for dynamic content like sidebars, login widgets, or shopping cart summaries.

data.title: Partial View and View Component

data.text: Razor Pages
Razor Pages organize UI code by page instead of controller. Each page has a `.cshtml` file and an optional PageModel class with handlers. Ideal for page-focused MVC apps.

data.title: Razor Page with PageModel

data.text: Entity Framework Core Migrations
EF Core Migrations track schema changes over time. Use `dotnet ef migrations add` and `dotnet ef database update` in development. For production, apply migrations programmatically on startup.

data.title: Migrations and Programmatic Updates

data.text: Minimal APIs
ASP.NET Core supports minimal API endpoints without controllers. Use `MapGet`, `MapPost`, `MapPut`, `MapDelete` for lightweight HTTP endpoints. Great for microservices or rapid prototyping.

data.title: Minimal API Endpoints

data.text: gRPC Basics
gRPC is a high-performance RPC framework using Protocol Buffers. Define services in `.proto` files, generate C# code, and implement services. ASP.NET Core hosts gRPC on HTTP/2.

data.title: gRPC Service Definition and Implementation

data.text: Localization

ASP.NET Core supports localized strings and culture-specific formatting. Configure supported cultures, add resource files, and use `IStringLocalizer` for translation. The request culture is determined from Accept-Language, query, or cookie.

data.title: Localization Setup and Usage

data.text: More Middleware Examples
Common middleware patterns include endpoint metadata, short-circuiting, and custom header manipulation. Use terminal middleware for health checks or static asset serving.

data.title: Advanced Middleware Patterns

data.text: More SignalR Examples
SignalR supports groups, streaming, client results, authorization, and reconnect logic. Use strong-typed hubs for compile safety. Configure JSON serialization for hub payloads.

data.title: SignalR Groups, Streaming, and Authorization

data.text: Output Caching

Output caching caches HTTP responses at the server level without changing application code. Available in .NET 8+. Use named policies or base policies to cache responses based on query, headers, or route values.

data.title: Output Caching Policies

data.text: Antiforgery and CSRF Protection

Antiforgery tokens prevent Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks. ASP.NET Core generates tokens automatically for form tag helpers and validates them on unsafe HTTP methods. Configure token header names for AJAX requests.

data.title: Antiforgery Configuration

data.text: Useful Built-in Services
ASP.NET Core ships with many useful services. Enable CORS, static files, WebSockets, output caching, response caching, request localization, rate limiting, and health checks as needed.

data.title: Common Service Registration Overview
